body:
## Problem

No contributor guide exists at `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md`. The repository enforces a build system (mise tasks), a test runner (`mise run test`), CI gates (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), and, with this change, a commit convention that release automation reads: svu computes each version from the commit types since the last tag.

## Evidence

`fd -H -d 3 -i '^contributing' .` returns nothing. `mise.toml:147` runs `tag=$(svu next --v0 --tag.pattern 'v*')`. svu 3.4.1 in a scratch repository: `fix:` → v0.1.1, `feat:` → v0.2.0, `feat!:`/`fix!:`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` → v0.2.0 with `--v0`, `chore:`/`ci:`/`docs:`/merge commits → no release. The commit rule is documented only in README.md "Releasing" (lines 243-248), which addresses the maintainer cutting a release, not a contributor writing a commit.

## Impact

A contributor who labels a refactor `feat:` or adds `!` to a subject changes the next version number, and nothing they are pointed to says so. Setup, test, lint and CI expectations are spread across README "Development" and CLAUDE.md with no contributor entry point.

## Fix

Scaffold `CONTRIBUTING.md` from this repository's sources only: intro (README title/description), development setup (`mise install`), build and test (`mise run build`, `mise run test`, `mise run all`), code style (`.editorconfig`, `.golangci.yml`, `mise run hooks:install`, `mise run lint:all`), commit convention (Conventional Commits; the svu bump table and its release consequence, pointing to README "Releasing"), pull-request process (the CI jobs in `ci.yml`: Build/vet/test, Test (macOS, Windows), Vulnerability scan, CodeQL), and license (MIT, `LICENSE`). Omit issue reporting: the repository has no issue templates and no SECURITY.md.

## Resolution
Added CONTRIBUTING.md built from repo sources only: setup (mise install), code style (.editorconfig, .golangci.yml, prek hooks), testing (mise tasks, git oracle), adding an internal/git reader (CLAUDE.md rules), commit messages (Conventional Commits; type decides the svu release, pointing to README Releasing), pull-request CI checks, MIT license. Issue reporting omitted: no templates, no SECURITY.md. markdownlint and editorconfig-checker pass.
title: No CONTRIBUTING.md, while commit types now decide release versions

body:
## Problem

The release task creates the annotated tag locally, then pushes it. When `git push origin "$tag"` fails, errexit stops the task with the tag still in the local repository.

## Evidence

`mise.toml:149` `git tag -a "$tag" -m "Release $tag"`, `mise.toml:150` `git push origin "$tag"`. On the next run svu reads local tags, so the unpushed tag at HEAD is the current version; with no commits after it, `svu next` prints that same tag (verified: a `ci:`-only range returns the current tag). `git tag -a` on an existing tag prints `fatal: tag 'v0.1.0' already exists` and exits 128 (verified in a scratch repository).

## Impact

After a network or authentication failure on push, rerunning `mise run release` prints "Releasing vX.Y.Z..." and then fails with "already exists", which says nothing about the unpushed tag. Recovery needs a manual `git push origin vX.Y.Z` or `git tag -d vX.Y.Z`.

## Fix

Remove the local tag when the push fails, so a rerun starts from the same state: replace line 150 with `if ! git push origin "$tag"; then git tag -d "$tag" >/dev/null; echo "Error: push failed; removed the local tag $tag" >&2; exit 1; fi` (as a multi-line if block).

## Resolution
mise.toml release task: a failed `git push origin "$tag"` now deletes the local tag and exits 1, and the comment says why. Verified in a throwaway clone with a failing-push git shim: the local tag is gone and svu computes the same version again (case 7); cases 1-6 unchanged; shellcheck clean.
title: A failed tag push leaves a local tag that blocks the next release run

body:
## Problem

The comment justifies the HEAD == origin/main check with "branch rulesets do not cover tags, so tagging unpushed work would publish it without a PR". This repository has no rulesets and no branch protection, so nothing requires a PR to reach main.

## Evidence

`mise.toml:125-127`: "HEAD must be exactly origin/main. A tag carries the commits it points at, and branch rulesets do not cover tags, so tagging unpushed work would publish it without a PR." `gh api repos/ivuorinen/git-dirty/rulesets?includes_parents=true` returns `[]`; `gh api repos/ivuorinen/git-dirty/branches/main/protection` returns "Branch not protected".

## Impact

A reader takes the comment to mean main is ruleset-protected and PR-gated, and may rely on that when reasoning about what a release can contain.

## Fix

State the reason that holds here: "HEAD must be exactly origin/main. A tag carries the commits it points at, so tagging unpushed work would publish commits that are not on main and that CI has not run on."

## Resolution
Release task comment now gives the reason that holds without rulesets: tagging unpushed work would publish commits that are not on main and that CI has not run on.
title: Release task comment cites branch rulesets the repository does not have

body:
## Problem

CLAUDE.md repeats the svu flags the release task passes, a second copy that must stay in step with `mise.toml`, and says `mise run release` "creates the next one" without saying the task cannot run until the first SemVer tag is made by hand.

## Evidence

`CLAUDE.md:124-125`: "`mise run release` creates the next one with svu (`--v0 --tag.pattern 'v*'`, so the old CalVer tag `2026.10.0` is ignored)." The flags live in `mise.toml:147`. With no v tag, the task stops with "no tags match 'v*'" (verified in a throwaway clone, case 1).

## Impact

A flag change in `mise.toml` leaves CLAUDE.md stale. An agent reading CLAUDE.md before v0.1.0 exists expects the task to work and meets svu's error instead.

## Fix

Replace the parenthetical with a pointer: "`mise run release` tags the next version with svu; the first SemVer tag is made by hand (README \"Releasing\")."

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md Build & Release drops the restated svu flags and says the first SemVer tag is made by hand, pointing to README "Releasing".
title: CLAUDE.md restates the svu flags and omits the hand-made first tag

body:
## Problem

With svu, the commit type of every change decides the next version. CLAUDE.md's "Rules that are easy to break" does not tell an agent writing commits in this repository.

## Evidence

`CLAUDE.md:73` "## Rules that are easy to break" lists internal/git, hostile clones, no runtime exec, golangci-lint, the git oracle, ahead/behind, global ignores and fuzzing; none covers commit types. svu 3.4.1 with `--v0`: `fix:` → patch, `feat:` → minor, `feat!:`/`fix!:`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` → minor, other types → no release (verified in a scratch repository).

## Impact

An agent that labels a refactor `feat:`, or marks a commit `!`, releases a minor version that no feature justifies.

## Fix

Add to "Rules that are easy to break": "- **Commit types set the release version.** svu reads them (README \"Releasing\"): `fix:` releases a patch, `feat:` a minor, `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` a minor while 0.x, and other types release nothing. Type a commit by what it changes for users."

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md "Rules that are easy to break" gains "Commit types set the release version", telling agents to type commits by what they change for users and pointing to README "Releasing" for the table instead of restating it.
title: Agent rules do not say that commit types now set the release version

body:
## Problem

The Releasing section says "The first releases had CalVer tags (`2026.10.0`)", plural, but the repository has one CalVer tag and one release.

## Evidence

`README.md:250`: "The first releases had CalVer tags (`2026.10.0`), which svu ignores." `git tag` lists only `2026.10.0`; `gh release list` lists only `2026.10.0`.

## Impact

A reader looks for other CalVer releases that do not exist.

## Fix

"The first release had a CalVer tag (`2026.10.0`), which svu ignores."

## Resolution
README.md: "The first release had a CalVer tag (`2026.10.0`)".
title: README says "the first releases" when one CalVer release exists

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. Known limitations claims: "A repository with `extensions.relativeWorktrees` is refused as an unknown extension."

## Evidence

`internal/git/format.go:17-19` lists it as known: `"relativeworktrees": true`, with the comment "worktree .git and gitdir files may hold relative paths, which findGitDir and readWorktree resolve". `TestCheckFormat` has the case "v1 relative worktrees" returning SHA1 (`internal/git/hash_test.go:84-90`), and `TestListWorktrees_RelativePaths` (`internal/git/worktree_test.go:246`) opens such a repository.

## Impact

The README tells users of `git worktree add --relative-paths` that their repositories show an error line. They are read normally.

## Fix

Delete the sentence "A repository with `extensions.relativeWorktrees` is refused as an unknown extension."

## Resolution
Removed the relativeWorktrees sentence from Known limitations in README.md.
title: README says relativeWorktrees repositories are refused

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. Actions claims: "Nothing can be typed: a remote needs ssh-agent or a credential helper. A key passphrase, an unknown host key or a password prompt makes the action fail with git's message."

## Evidence

`environ` (`internal/action/run.go:91-101`) strips only git's repository-local variables and sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`; `GIT_ASKPASS` and `SSH_ASKPASS` stay in the environment, and `core.askPass` comes from git config. Reproduced with git 2.56.0: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_ASKPASS=<script> git fetch --all` with stdin on the null device, against a local HTTP server answering 401. git ran the script for "Username for ..." and "Password for ...", and sent the answers as an Authorization header.

## Impact

A user with an askpass program expects an action to fail at once. A window opens instead, and the action, or a mass run, waits for it.

## Fix

Replace with: "Nothing can be typed in the TUI: a remote needs ssh-agent, a credential helper or an askpass program (`GIT_ASKPASS`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `core.askPass`), which opens its own window and holds the action until it is answered. Without one, a key passphrase, an unknown host key or a password prompt makes the action fail with git's message."

## Resolution
README Actions now names askpass programs and says they hold the action until answered.
title: README says credential prompts always fail, askpass still prompts

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. `Run` claims: "git starts without a terminal and with stdin on the null device, so neither git nor ssh can prompt: a credential that needs typing fails with git's own message." `environ` (lines 89-90) claims GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 is set "so git does not ask for a username or password."

## Evidence

`environ` keeps `GIT_ASKPASS` and `SSH_ASKPASS`. With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, stdin on the null device and `GIT_ASKPASS` set, git 2.56.0 called the askpass program for the username and the password against a 401 HTTP remote. `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` only stops the terminal prompt.

## Impact

The comment states a guarantee the code does not give, in the one package allowed to run programs. A reader auditing what an action can block on is told it cannot block on a prompt.

## Fix

Line 68-70: "so neither git nor ssh can prompt on a terminal: a credential that needs typing fails with git's own message, unless an askpass program the user configured answers it." Line 89-90: "so git does not ask on a terminal for a username or password."

## Resolution
Run's and environ's docstrings now limit the claim to terminal prompts and name the askpass exception.
title: Run's docstring says neither git nor ssh can prompt

body:
## Problem

Contradiction. `modified` claims: "ex is needed for submodules, whose untracked files make them modified."

## Evidence

`submoduleChanged` (`internal/gitstat/dirty.go:351-355`) states the opposite: "Untracked files inside it do not count; `git diff --quiet` ignores them." Its body calls only `sub.modified` and `sub.staged`, and nothing on that path reads `ex`. The git oracle agrees with `submoduleChanged`: with an untracked file in a clean submodule, git 2.56.0's `git diff --quiet` exits 0.

## Impact

A maintainer trusting the docstring would add an untracked check to submodules and make `M` disagree with `git diff --quiet`, the test oracle.

## Fix

Delete the sentence "ex is needed for submodules, whose untracked files make them modified."

## Resolution
Removed the sentence about untracked files in submodules from modified's docstring. The unused ex parameter routes to /nitpicker dead-code.
title: modified's docstring contradicts submoduleChanged on untracked files

body:
## Problem

Stale. `Open` claims: "The path must contain a .git directory, or a .git file ("gitdir: <path>") as written for linked worktrees and absorbed submodules."

## Evidence

`Open` calls `gitrepo.OpenWorktree`, whose docstring (`internal/git/repository.go:39-42`) also accepts "a folder that is itself a git directory, which has no working tree and is opened as bare". `Inspect` relies on that for bare repositories (`internal/gitstat/inspect.go:46-48`), and `TestInspect_Bare` covers it.

## Impact

The word "must" tells a caller a bare repository is rejected. It is the path every bare repository takes.

## Fix

"Open opens the repository at path: a working tree holding a .git directory or a .git file ("gitdir: <path>"), as written for linked worktrees and absorbed submodules, or a folder that is itself a git directory, which is opened as bare."

## Resolution
gitstat.Open's docstring now includes a folder that is itself a git directory.
title: gitstat.Open's docstring omits bare repositories

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The field comment claims: "branch names treated as the default when origin/HEAD is absent".

## Evidence

`defaultBranchName` (`internal/gitstat/refs.go:118-142`) reads `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, and `defaultRemote` (`internal/gitstat/refs.go:177-187`) picks the checked-out branch's upstream remote, falling back to `origin` only without one.

## Impact

For a branch tracking another remote, the list is used when that remote's HEAD is absent, even if `origin/HEAD` exists.

## Fix

"branch names treated as the default when refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD is absent"

## Resolution
MainBranches comment now says refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD.
title: MainBranches comment names origin/HEAD for any remote

body:
## Problem

Stale. The package docstring claims: "Its fetch and pull keys run git through internal/action; everything else only reads."

## Evidence

`saveSettings` (`internal/tui/settings.go:232-240`) writes the config file through `m.cfg.Save`, which defaults to `config.Save`, on `ctrl+s`.

## Impact

A reader scoping what the TUI can change is told it writes nothing outside git.

## Fix

"Its fetch and pull keys run git through internal/action, and its settings page writes the config file; everything else only reads."

## Resolution
Package tui's docstring now names the settings page writing the config file.
title: Package tui says everything but fetch and pull only reads

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. Settings page claims: "`ctrl+s` checks the settings as startup does (a missing `dir` is an error)".

## Evidence

`session.reconfigure` (`main.go:181-188`) first runs `Normalize` on the file layer, which startup does not: with `-m 4`, startup accepts `maxDepth` 0 and a save refuses it. Its comment says so, and `TestSession_ReconfigureChecksTheFileLayer` asserts both. `tuiConfig` (`main.go:150-160`) runs `checkDir` on the directory in effect, so a missing `dir` under a directory argument saves without error, as the same test asserts.

## Impact

A user with a flag set sees a save refused for a value the README says startup would accept, and a missing `dir` accepted where the README says it is an error.

## Fix

"`ctrl+s` checks the edited values, then the settings in effect as startup does (a missing directory is an error, unless the environment or a directory argument names another one), writes the file and rescans with them; on an error nothing is written."

## Resolution
README's ctrl+s description now covers the check of the form's values and the directory in effect.
title: README's ctrl+s description no longer matches reconfigure

body:
## Problem

Missing. The Usage flag table lists every flag except `--config FILE`.

## Evidence

`parseArgs` defines it (`main.go:503`: `fs.StringVar(&opts.configPath, "config", "", "")`), and `writeHelp` lists it (`main.go:572-573`). The README mentions it only in prose under Configuration (line 186).

## Impact

A reader of the flag table does not learn the flag exists.

## Fix

Add before `--version`: "| `--config FILE` | Read settings from FILE, and save them there, instead of the default file |".

## Resolution
Added --config FILE to README's flag table.
title: README's flag table omits --config

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The introduction claims: "On a terminal it opens an interactive browser. When its output is piped, or with `--plain`, it prints the report."

## Evidence

`useTUI` (`main.go:232-234`) is `interactive && stdinTTY && stdoutTTY && term != "dumb"`. `echo | git-dirty` on a terminal, `TERM=dumb git-dirty`, and `"interactive": false` in the config file all print the report.

## Impact

Those three cases contradict the sentence, and piped stdin looks like a bug.

## Fix

"When stdin and stdout are terminals and `TERM` is not `dumb`, it opens an interactive browser. Otherwise, or with `--plain` or `\"interactive\": false`, it prints the report."

## Resolution
README's introduction now states useTUI's conditions.
title: README understates when the plain report is printed

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The line table claims the comparison is against "(`origin/main` when it exists, else the local `main`)".

## Evidence

`versusRef` (`internal/gitstat/refs.go:208-219`) uses `refs/remotes/<remote>/<name>`, and `defaultRemote` (`internal/gitstat/refs.go:179-187`) is the checked-out branch's upstream remote, else `origin`.

## Impact

On a branch tracking `upstream`, the counts are against `upstream/main`, not the `origin/main` the README names.

## Fix

"(`<remote>/main`, with the remote chosen as described below, when it exists, else the local `main`)".

## Resolution
README's line table now says <remote>/main.
title: README names origin/main for the comparison on any remote

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The sample tree shows: "⚠️ broken ! index: unknown extension".

## Evidence

The only index extension error is `unsupported index extension %q` (`internal/git/index.go:292`), which README line 285 quotes correctly as `! index: unsupported index extension "sdir"`.

## Impact

The sample and the Known limitations section disagree on the same error.

## Fix

"│   └── ⚠️ broken ! index: unsupported index extension \"sdir\""

## Resolution
README's sample tree now shows the program's index extension error.
title: README's sample output shows an error the program cannot print

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. Claims: "`core.excludesFile` (default `~/.config/git/ignore`)".

## Evidence

`LoadExcludes` (`internal/gitstat/ignore.go:25-36`) defaults to `filepath.Join(xdg, "git", "ignore")`, where `xdg` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, or `~/.config` when unset.

## Impact

With `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set, the file read is not the one the README names.

## Fix

"`core.excludesFile` (default `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore`, `~/.config/git/ignore` when that is unset)".

## Resolution
README gives $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore as the default, with the fallback when it is unset.
title: README gives a fixed default for the global ignore file

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The differences table claims: "`-p` needs GNU parallel".

## Evidence

`scripts/git-dirty.sh:565-576` falls back: "Parallel not found. Using manual parallelization...". Run on a two-repository tree with no `parallel` on `PATH`, `scripts/git-dirty.sh -p` printed that line, listed both repositories and exited 0.

## Impact

The table misstates what the replaced script required.

## Fix

"`-p` uses GNU parallel when installed, else its own parallel jobs".

## Resolution
README's differences table now says the script uses GNU parallel when installed, else its own jobs.
title: README says the bash script's -p needs GNU parallel

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The differences table claims: "`-t` has no visible effect".

## Evidence

Under `-p`, `scripts/git-dirty.sh:838-846` computes the indent from the full path when truncation is off. On a test tree, `-p` printed "   ✅ one" and `-p -t` printed "                   ✅ one". Without `-p`, the output is identical, as `print_result` prints only the basename.

## Impact

The table is true only without `-p`.

## Fix

"`-t` has no visible effect without `-p`; with it, it only deepens the indentation".

## Resolution
README's differences table now limits the -t claim to runs without -p.
title: README says the bash script's -t has no visible effect

body:
## Problem

Incorrect structure. `### Settings page` (line 223) was inserted in the middle of `## Configuration`, so the paragraphs at lines 243-259 ("A directory is skipped when...", linked worktrees, "Ignore rules follow git's") fall under it.

## Evidence

Those paragraphs describe the scan and apply with no settings page involved: `skipReason` (`internal/scan/scan.go:240-251`), `discoverer.worktree` (`internal/scan/scan.go:193-208`), `LoadExcludes` (`internal/gitstat/ignore.go:23`).

## Impact

A reader looking for what is skipped does not look under Settings page, and a link to `#settings-page` lands on unrelated text after the form's description.

## Fix

Move lines 223-241 (the `### Settings page` heading and its three paragraphs) after line 259, so the scan paragraphs stay directly under `## Configuration`.

## Resolution
Moved README's Settings page section after the scan paragraphs; the #settings-page anchor still resolves.
title: Scan rules sit under README's Settings page heading

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. Claims `LoadExcludes` "reads both `~/.config/git/config` and `~/.gitconfig` and defaults to `~/.config/git/ignore`, as git does."

## Evidence

`globalConfigFiles` (`internal/gitstat/ignore.go:53-69`) also reads `/etc/gitconfig` unless `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` is set, replaces the global files with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` when set, and uses `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in place of `~/.config`. The default is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore` (lines 25-36).

## Impact

This file lists rules that are easy to break. An edit made from this description would drop the system config, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` or XDG handling.

## Fix

"which reads the system config (unless `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`), then `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` or else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config` and `~/.gitconfig`, and defaults to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore`, as git does."

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md now lists the system config, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and XDG handling of LoadExcludes.
title: CLAUDE.md understates what LoadExcludes reads

body:
## Problem

Outdated architecture. The map attributes "format check" to `repository.go` and does not list `format.go` or `hash.go`.

## Evidence

`checkFormat` and `knownExtensions` are in `internal/git/format.go:11-46`; `repository.go:84` only calls it. `ObjectID`, `Format` and the object hashing are in `internal/git/hash.go`.

## Impact

The list of repository extensions the readers accept, a limit on what a hostile clone can reach, is not where the map says.

## Fix

"`repository.go` (git dir, commondir; `IsGitDir`, ...)", and add "`format.go` (repository format version, `knownExtensions`), `hash.go` (object IDs and hashing)".

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md's internal/git map now lists format.go and hash.go.
title: CLAUDE.md's internal/git map omits format.go and hash.go

body:
## Problem

Missing. The description of `proc_unix.go` is "`Setsid`, and SIGINT to the process group on cancel".

## Evidence

`Run` calls `reap` after a cancel (`internal/action/run.go:82-84`), and `reap` sends SIGKILL to the process group (`internal/action/proc_unix.go:29-38`); on Windows it does nothing (`internal/action/proc_windows.go:23-25`).

## Impact

An edit to the cancel path made from this description would not account for the SIGKILL that follows git's exit.

## Fix

"(`proc_unix.go`: `Setsid`, SIGINT to the process group on cancel, and `reap`'s SIGKILL to what is left of it once git has exited; ...)".

## Resolution
CLAUDE.md's proc_unix.go description now includes reap's SIGKILL.
title: CLAUDE.md's internal/action description omits reap

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. Claims: "shortHashLen matches git's minimum abbreviation."

## Evidence

git's minimum is 4 (git-config(1), `core.abbrev`: "The minimum length is 4"). 7 is the length git uses by default before scaling up for large repositories.

## Impact

The constant's stated reason is wrong, though its value is the common display length.

## Fix

"shortHashLen matches git's default abbreviation for small repositories."

## Resolution
shortHashLen's comment now says git's default abbreviation for small repositories.
title: shortHashLen comment calls 7 git's minimum abbreviation

body:
## Problem

Stale. `docs/plans/2026-11-07-tui-git-actions-and-settings.md:4` claims "Status: ACCEPTED 2026-11-07 — awaiting the go-ahead to implement". `docs/plans/2026-10-22-drop-go-git.md:4` and `docs/plans/2026-10-22-git-dirty-go.md:4` claim "Status: DRAFT — awaiting approval to implement".

## Evidence

All three are implemented: `go.mod` has no go-git or go-billy module and `internal/git` reads git storage in-tree; `main.go` is the Go program; `internal/tui/mass.go`, `settings.go` and `internal/action` carry out the 2026-11-07 plan. `docs/plans/2026-11-01-bare-repositories-design.md:4` shows the form these should take: "APPROVED 2026-11-01, implemented on feat/bare-repositories".

## Impact

A reader of the plans cannot tell which were carried out.

## Fix

Change each status line to say it is implemented, as the bare-repositories design does. Replace nothing else in the plans: they record what was decided at the time.

## Resolution
Status lines of the three plans now say they are implemented.
title: Three implemented plans still say they await approval

body:
## Problem

Missing. Nine exported methods have no doc comment.

## Evidence

An AST pass over every non-test Go file reports: `main.go:450` `String` and `main.go:452` `Set` (`excludeValue`), `internal/action/run.go:122` `Write` (`tail`), `internal/git/hash.go:58` `String` (`ObjectType`), `internal/git/hash.go:132` `Write` (`ObjectHasher`), and `internal/gitstat/aheadbehind.go:245-247,258` `Len`, `Less`, `Swap`, `Pop` (`commitQueue`). The adjacent `Push` at `internal/gitstat/aheadbehind.go:249` has one.

## Impact

Each implements a standard interface, so the cost is small; `commitQueue.Push` shows the documented form, and the set is inconsistent with it.

## Fix

Add a one-line comment to each naming the interface it implements, as `Push` does ("Pop implements heap.Interface").

## Resolution
Added doc comments to all nine exported methods.
title: Nine exported methods have no doc comment

body:
## Problem

Test name misrepresents behavior. `TestIgnore_NoSystemConfigRead` claims the system config is not read.

## Evidence

The body checks that `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` is set and that `LoadExcludes` returns no error. Nothing asserts what was read: removing the `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` check in `globalConfigFiles` (`internal/gitstat/ignore.go:55`) leaves the test passing wherever `/etc/gitconfig` holds no bad config.

## Impact

The name reads as coverage of the `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` rule, which the test does not exercise.

## Fix

Rename to `TestIgnore_LoadsWithNoSystemConfig`, which is what its own comment describes ("a missing system file must not be an error either way").

## Resolution
Renamed the test to TestIgnore_LoadsWithNoSystemConfig.
title: TestIgnore_NoSystemConfigRead does not test what it is named for

body:
## Problem

Incorrect. The help claims "-p  Process directories in parallel (requires 'parallel' command)" (line 975; also the `#USAGE` line 5) and "-d NUM  Set maximum depth for showing non-git directories" (line 974; also the `#USAGE` line 10).

## Evidence

`process_in_parallel` falls back at lines 565-576 ("Parallel not found. Using manual parallelization..."); run with no `parallel` on `PATH`, `-p` listed both test repositories and exited 0. `GIT_DIRTY_DEPTH` is assigned at lines 41 and 1034 and read only in the help text at line 974, so `-d` changes nothing, as README line 270 records.

## Impact

The script is the reference for `bench` and `compare.sh`, and its help is where README line 269's wrong `-p` claim comes from.

## Fix

Change the text only, because `bench` and `compare.sh` depend on the script's behavior. Lines 5 and 975: "Process directories in parallel (GNU parallel when installed)". Lines 10 and 974: say that the value is accepted and has no effect.

## Resolution
The bash script's help and #USAGE lines now describe -p and -d correctly; only text changed.
title: The bash script's help misstates -p and -d

body:
## Problem

Stale. The header claims: "The script automatically skips folders: node_modules, vendor".

## Evidence

The default at line 45 is `GIT_DIRTY_EXCLUDE:=node_modules vendor .cache build dist .tests .test`, and `internal/config/config.go:43` carries the same seven.

## Impact

A reader of the reference script undercounts what it skips when comparing results with git-dirty.

## Fix

Line 28: "#   node_modules, vendor, .cache, build, dist, .tests, .test (GIT_DIRTY_EXCLUDE)".

## Resolution
The bash script's header now lists all seven excluded folders.
title: The bash script's header lists two of seven excluded folders
